premise: I poured my $108,000 nursing pension into purchasing and restoring a historic 1920s greenhouse and rare orchid conservatory with my brother, who signed a notarized 40% stake and a lifetime of weekly orchid deliveries for my church; when a botanical garden consortium offered $680,000 for the orchid collection and property he forged a dissolution, sold my share, and handed me a $5,000 “plant food” check—I found the original agreement sealed in a glass cloche under a prized cattleya, voided the sale, and now run ‘Bloom of Deceit Orchids,’ where he repots specimens in a vest that says ‘Rooted in Fraud’ and every plant tag prints the probate case number.
